questions.answer: Yes. FEAT-004 is optional only in the sense that it is present when PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE=1 is chosen. When selected, REQ-HS-001 makes the four-phase handshake mandatory. HS_TYPE values other than 0 or 1 are illegal and their behavior is not specified or checked.

CELL_TYPE=0 is inside the stated range 0 to 4. It means bypass with no synchronizer stage, for simulation only. It must not be used in a netlist, and the SDC rejects it (depth below 2). The test plan covers CELL_TYPE 1 to 4 only.
The APB5 ports are present in every configuration of the RTL top. In APB4 the unused inputs are ignored and the unused outputs are 0, so they are tied off, not removed.

In both modes PREADY is a one-cycle pulse in state RESP, and the FSM then returns to IDLE and can capture the next Setup in the following cycle. In two-phase the acknowledge event itself leads to PREADY, and request and acknowledge are equal when idle. In four-phase PREADY is delayed until the acknowledge has fallen, so the handshake is closed before the next Setup. The PREADY pulse behaves the same in both modes. Only the latency differs.

'Stable' means the last value is held, not forced to zero. Registers reset to 0, PRDATA holds its value until the next response, and PSLVERR is cleared after the PREADY cycle. The completer-side fields such as PADDR keep the last bundle value when idle.
PAUSER and PWUSER are functionally meaningful only in APB5 with a width above 0. The ports exist in the top in every configuration, and in APB4 they are ignored and the outputs are 0.

The term is the in-progress term of the completer-side FSM. o_apb_pwakeup is a flip-flop that must be high no later than o_apb_psel. It falls one cycle after the transfer ends, which is when psel and penable drop at the PREADY edge. It is high whenever the synchronized wake-up is high or a transfer is in progress.
The state is not specified. A single reset is unsupported, is not detected, and is not tested. TEST-012 resets both domains together.

CFG-MIN derives from the configuration CFG-APB4. The other configurations use the same pattern ('CFG-APB4 plus ...'). ADDR_W=1 is legal, because the range is 1 to 32 and only 0 is illegal. CFG-MIN is the smallest legal instance.

Yes, they are consistent. ADDR_W=1 and DATA_W=8 are inside the legal ranges. The user widths are 0 with APB5=0, so none of the listed illegal combinations applies. FEAT-004, FEAT-006 and FEAT-007 are absent by parameters.

The slv FSM looks for a request event only in IDLE. SETUP always goes to ACCESS, and PENABLE rises one cycle after PSEL. A new request cannot arrive earlier, because APB is non-pipelined and the bridge carries one transfer at a time. A zero-wait PREADY in the first Access cycle is legal.

The premise is wrong, because these signals are in the port table. i_apb_pwakeup and o_apb_pwakeup are CFG-APB5 and cross through the synchronizer. PRUSER and PBUSER (i_ and o_) are CFG-USER and travel in the response bundle. They are passed through unchanged.

There is no conflict. 'Should provide all user signals' is a recommendation restated from REF-001. The bridge provides all four user signals in configurations with APB5=1 and width above 0. A width of 0 means the signal is not present.
The bridge does not check or force PSTRB. It forwards PSTRB as received, including a non-zero value in a read, regardless of PWRITE.

Yes. A transfer in flight at reset is lost, and both resets must be asserted together. While reset is asserted, every register is at its reset value. After release the test expects state cleared and the transfer repeated correctly (the repeat is done by the requester model).

It is selected by PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE. 0 gives toggle (two-phase) and 1 gives level (four-phase). The request event is: two-phase, synchronized request different from reg_ack (slv side); four-phase, synchronized request high. The ack event on the mst side is: two-phase, synchronized ack equal to reg_req; four-phase, synchronized ack high.

It is an integration assumption outside the IP, not logic the IP implements. The resets are asserted together and released synchronously outside the IP. REQ-RESET-002 and ASM-002 state this, and there is no reset synchronizer inside. The testbench requester keeping PSEL low is only the verification model.

The document is internally inconsistent. The formula ADDR_W+3+1+STRB_W+DATA_W gives a minimum of 14 for ADDR_W=1 and DATA_W=8, but 'at least 7' is stated. The designer must say whether the stated minimum or the formula is correct. (LPARA_RESP_W minimum 9 is consistent.)
Yes, non-multiples of 8 are legal. The legal range is 0 to DATA_W, a multiple of 8 is only recommended, and non-multiples are not in the illegal list.

No check is expected. The IP has no elaboration check for illegal values, and their behavior is unspecified. REQ-PARAM-001 only requires accepting the legal values, which are verified by elaborating the legal extremes.

Yes, both are 0 at reset. In two-phase the request and acknowledge bits are equal when idle, and at reset both are 0. Between transfers they are equal and not necessarily 0. In four-phase both are 0 when idle.

The bound follows the handshake type. HS_TYPE 0 uses REQ-PERF-001, (N+3)T_mst+(N+3+w)T_slv. HS_TYPE 1 uses REQ-PERF-002, (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv. OP-001 and OP-002 cite whichever applies to the configuration. OP-009 is the four-phase case, so REQ-PERF-002.
Yes. o_apb_pwakeup is high whenever the synchronized wake-up is high or a transfer is in progress. It stays high until PREADY when high with PSEL, falls one cycle after the transfer, and resets to 0.

Yes, it is included. D is measured from Setup to the end of the PREADY cycle, and PREADY is raised only after the acknowledge has fallen (CLOSE/REQ0). The equal-clock figure 4N+8+w matches the measurement (16 for N=2). With unequal clocks the bound is the sum (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv.

The document does not use 'interconnect'. The bridge is an APB completer on the requester-side interface and an APB requester on the completer-side interface. The behavior is attributed to the bridge or IP, and the requester model in the testbench.

Yes, both resets are asserted together, as REQ-RESET-002 requires. The repeat of the transfer is done by the requester model of the verification, not by the bridge. The bridge only loses the in-flight transfer.

N is the number of synchronizer stages (2, 2, 3, 4 for CELL_TYPE 1 to 4). w is the number of completer wait states. T_mst and T_slv are the clock periods. The duration D runs from the first cycle of the Setup phase to the end of the PREADY cycle on the requester side. The limit includes the wait states through the w term.

It refers to the requester-side clock (i_clk_mst): the Setup is accepted in the cycle after the PREADY cycle. By then the handshake has completed, because PREADY is raised only after the acknowledge event (four-phase: after it has returned to 0). So it does not conflict with the multi-cycle duration limit, which is the time per transfer.
The rule holds. The wrapper reset value PARA_APBCDC_CELL_RST_VAL is 0 for all control bits of this IP. The synchronizer stages reset to 0, so every flop resets to 0.

DEC-021 is this: the RTL top declares the APB5 ports in every configuration, with widths of at least 1 for absent user signals, unused inputs ignored and unused outputs 0. This is because SystemVerilog has no optional ports. It deviates from PRT-03 and is recorded in the module header.

Two-phase (HS_TYPE 0): duration at most (N+3)T_mst+(N+3+w)T_slv. Four-phase (HS_TYPE 1): at most (2N+4)T_mst+(2N+4+w)T_slv. They apply as in the answer to Q25, with N, w and T as defined for REQ-PERF-001/002. Example, equal clocks: 2N+6+w and 4N+8+w cycles.

The document contradicts itself. Assertions are disabled while either reset is asserted, except SVA-016. SVA-007 is described as also holding 'in reset', yet it is not exempted. It does not say which reset (mst, slv, or both) enables SVA-016, or what applies to SVA-007 in reset. The designer must resolve this.
The quick run is reported with 64 runs, 0 failures, assertion failures 0 and assertions never exercised 0. The pass criterion is therefore zero failures and every assertion exercised at least once.

It is binding. 'Shall' is defined as mandatory and testable, and the sentence says the RTL shall contain no latch, combinational loop, tri-state, clock gating or derived clock. 'Not required' refers to the detailed DFT specification.
It is binding through the port list. The IP has no DFT ports and the port list has no test ports, and REQ-IF-001 requires exactly the ports of 6.2. The test-reset override belongs to the SoC wrapper.

The two statements conflict. 17.1.2 says the placement 'should' keep each launch flop and first synchronizer stage adjacent, while 17.2 says it 'shall'. The document does not reconcile them, so the designer must say which strength applies.

The values are given: for N=2, T_mst=10 ns and T_slv=20 ns, EXC-001 is 20 ns, EXC-002 20 ns, EXC-003 10 ns, EXC-004 10 ns and EXC-005 20 ns. 'The same two commands' means set_max_delay -ignore_clock_latency plus set_false_path -hold. However, whether the hold check is really disabled in a Synopsys sign-off tool (and the semantics and priority of the exceptions) is explicitly unconfirmed (OI-004).

The guard band is one period of the destination clock of each crossing. For mst-to-slv crossings it is T_slv, and for slv-to-mst crossings it is T_mst. That is why the budgets are (N-1)xT_slv for the request bundle and (N-1)xT_mst for the response bundle.

The document says only that the slv clock controller must act on i_apb_pwakeup (or a requester signal) before the request arrives, and that ASM-005 assumes the controller keeps i_clk_slv running. OI-002 is still marked 'Clarify with the designer' and ASM-005 is Open. Missing: the designer's decision on which party guarantees the clock.

The document does not say. DEC-019 and DEC-020 are the author's unconfirmed choices (the RTL was written with them), while REQ-FUNC-004 and REQ-HS-004 are written as 'shall'. Missing: designer confirmation of whether they are binding.

DEC-021 is the author's unconfirmed choice, and OI-005 asks the designer to confirm it or deliver two tops. The document does not record acceptance. It also does not settle whether it conflicts with DEC-003 (one parameter selects APB4/APB5). Missing: the designer's confirmation.
